steps.title: Produce lentivirus by 293T transfection
steps.instruction: Transfect 293T cells at ~80% confluence on a 15‑cm plate using PEI to generate lentiviral particles.

substeps.instruction: a. Grow 293T cells to ~80% confluence on a 15‑cm plate.
b. Thaw and pre‑warm PEI (Polysciences, #23966‑2) and Opti‑MEM at 37 °C.
c. Prepare DNA mixture in a 15 mL conical tube: 8.1 µg MDL, 3.1 µg Rev, 4.1 µg VSVG, 12.2 µg ATP6V1Ai_1 in 250 µL Opti‑MEM.
d. Prepare PEI mixture: 110 µL PEI in 250 µL Opti‑MEM.
e. Add the PEI mixture dropwise to the DNA mixture (1:1 volume), gently agitate to avoid white precipitate, swirl 5×, invert 5×, vortex 10 s.
f. Incubate the PEI/DNA solution 15 min at room temperature (20‑25 °C) until translucent.
g. Add ~700 µL of the transfection mix to the 15‑cm plate and return to the incubator.
h. After 6‑8 h, replace the medium with 15 mL fresh growth medium.
i. After 48 h, collect the first batch of viral supernatant into a sterile 50 mL conical tube.
j. Add another 15 mL of fresh medium to the plate and incubate for 24 h.
k. Collect the second batch of viral supernatant into a sterile 50 mL conical tube.
l. Discard the 293T plate after treating it with 10 % bleach for 10 min, then dispose of it in a biohazard container.
m. Filter each harvested supernatant through a 0.22 µm pore‑size filter into a sterile container.
n. Keep filtered viral media on ice at 4 °C and use within 3 days.

steps.title: Concentrate lentivirus by ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Pellet and resuspend lentiviral particles from filtered supernatant using a refrigerated ultracentrifuge.

substeps.instruction: a. Install the appropriate rotor (Beckman L‑100XP or Optima XE‑90 with 32 SW‑Ti) and pre‑cool the ultracentrifuge to 4 °C.
b. In the biosafety cabinet, place empty 38.5‑mL polypropylene tubes into the metal rotor tubes using sterile forceps.
c. Cap the metal tubes and chill the assembly at 4 °C for 15 min.
d. Transfer 25–38 mL of the filtered viral media (from step 1) into each polypropylene tube.
e. Recap the metal tubes, bring them back to the ultracentrifuge, and balance the rotor.
f. Centrifuge at 45,891 × g, 4 °C for 2 h.
g. Return the rotor to the BSC, open the metal tubes, and remove the polypropylene tubes with sterile forceps.
h. Aspirate the supernatant from each polypropylene tube by gently tilting; avoid disturbing the pellet.
i. Gently resuspend the invisible virus pellet in 500 µL DMEM (or medium of choice), limiting pipette up‑and‑down actions to ≤10.
j. Transfer the resuspended virus to a sterile 15 mL conical tube or 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
k. Centrifuge at 3,000 × g for 5 min to pellet residual debris.
l. Aliquot the clarified supernatant into 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
m. Store aliquots at –80 °C; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles (single cycle can cut infectivity by ~50 %).

steps.title: Titrate lentivirus using qPCR
steps.instruction: Determine viral particle concentration with the ABM qPCR lentivirus titration kit.

substeps.instruction: a. Dilute virus 1:10: add 2 µL concentrated lentivirus to 18 µL PBS in a 0.5 mL tube.
b. Further dilute 1:10 in lysis buffer: add 2 µL of the 1:10 dilution to 18 µL Virus Lysis Buffer; mix gently by swirling or tapping.
c. Incubate the lysate at room temperature (20‑25 °C) for 3 min (this is the ‘viral lysate’).
d. Prepare qPCR reactions in triplicate for each of: viral lysate, standard 1 (STD1), standard 2 (STD2), and a no‑template control (NTC). For each 25 µL reaction add:
• 12.5 µL 2× SYBR‑Green master mix,
• 2.5 µL appropriate template (viral lysate, STD1, STD2, or 2.5 µL DMEM for NTC),
• 10 µL reagent‑mix (as supplied).
e. Run the real‑time PCR with the following program:
1) 42 °C for 20 min (reverse transcription),
2) 95 °C for 10 min (enzyme activation),
3) 95 °C for 15 s (denaturation),
4) 60 °C for 1 min (annealing/extension).
